title: Priv: IAM scaffolding & least-privilege policy factory (terraform module + audit hooks)
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and companion automation that scaffolds IAM/RBAC for Private (VPC) deployments, produces least-privilege role/policy templates, and wires audit and health-check hooks into our runtime. Goal: provide a simple input surface for teams to declare service boundaries and have the module emit roles, policies, bindings, and drift-detection alerts that are safe for production upgrades and automated rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a small set of inputs: service_name, principal_map (service_account/service_role), allowed_actions whitelist, resource_prefix, environment tags
Generated IAM roles/policies follow least-privilege defaults with documented opt-outs
Module includes a migration plan for existing roles (rename / replicate / phased-cutover) and a tested upgrade script
Automated health checks validate: role bindings, policy attachment, IAM condition syntax, and a basic permission probe (read-only) run in CI
Module produces a report artifact (JSON) suitable for Console ingestion showing policy delta and estimated privilege surface
Security review sign-off obtained and playbook for emergency rollback exists
tasks: Design variable schema and examples for internal teams (v1 and v2 backwards-compatible inputs)
Implement Terraform module: roles, policies, bindings, condition templates, and examples for AWS/GCP/Azure where applicable
Add automated policy sanitizer that rewrites wide statements into explicit allow lists or denies with IAM conditions
Build an upgrade script that can run in CI and create a migration plan PR with diffs
Wire health-checks: periodic CI job and runtime probe that exercises a minimal permission set
Create Confluence design doc and public docs in /docs/internal/priv-iam
Create GitHub repo skeleton, write unit tests for Terraform with terratest or kitchen-terraform
Run security review and iterate on feedback
updates: 2026-02-15: Ticket opened by Ayesha Malik. Draft goals and initial scope created.
2026-02-20: Architecture sync with Infra and Security. Decided to support both cloud-native IAM and an abstract RBAC mapping for on-prem service mesh identities.
2026-02-27: RFC (confluence) shared: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Priv+IAM+Policy+Factory. Feedback requested from SecOps.
2026-03-04: Spike completed: proof-of-concept generates role + limited policy and a JSON report. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-iam-module/pull/12
2026-03-07: Security review flagged long policy statements — implemented sanitizer prototype that converts '*' actions into explicit lists or requires a justification tag.
2026-03-10: Module API stabilized. Began writing terratest suite and health-check probe. Assigned to Lucas for implementation of upgrade plan and CI integration.
notes: Trade-offs: allowing fully custom policy blobs gives flexibility but hides privilege surface. Default will generate explicit allow lists; provide opt-in raw_policy flag requiring audited justification.
We prefer staged cutover (duplicate role -> attach new role to new service account -> cut traffic -> retire old role) for minimal blast radius.
Telemetry: the module should emit a compact JSON report with counts of broad grants and used-by estimates so Console can surface regressions during rollouts.
Open question: whether to include OPA policy generation for runtime RBAC or leave that to platform teams. Proposal: emit OPA snippets as optional output but not enforce them in v1.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy sanitizer: input fuzzing for wide statements and expected normalized output
Terratest integration: create ephemeral infra in test account, apply module, verify role/policy/binding, run permission probe, destroy
Upgrade test: simulate existing role with traffic, run migration plan to new role and validate zero-downtime cutover in staging
CI gate: require JSON report artifact and no broad grants flagged before merge
Manual review: Security must approve any opt-out raw_policy usage with ticketed justification
